articles.headline: After dueling late 60-yard field goals, No. 4 Indiana escapes Minnesota's upset bid in OT
keyFacts: Indiana defeated Minnesota 23-16 in overtime after kickers Luke Drzewiecki and Paddy McAteer both made 60-yard field goals in the final seconds of regulation.
Charlie Becker caught a 25-yard touchdown pass from Grant Wilson on the first play of overtime to give Indiana the lead.
Indiana's defense stopped Minnesota on fourth down during the extra period to secure the program's 29th consecutive win against an unranked opponent.
body: On a nightmarish special teams day, Indiana got an incredible kick to avoid a second loss of the season.

Seconds after Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki hit a go-ahead 60-yard field goal to put the Gophers up 16-13, Paddy McAteer drained a kick of the same length as time expired in the fourth quarter to get the game to overtime.

From there, Charlie Becker caught a 25-yard pass from Grant Wilson on the first play of the extra period and the Indiana defense prevented Minnesota from getting into the end zone in the Hoosiers' 23-16 win.
Minnesota got inside the Indiana 5-yard line on its overtime possession, but Drake Lindsey was sacked on fourth down after he scrambled for no gain on third down.
The Gophers entered the game as 20.5-point underdogs and the win is Indiana's 29th consecutive against an unranked opponent.
"This is entertainment, so we thought we'd put some entertainment value into this game," Indiana coach Curt Cignetti deadpanned after the game.

articles.headline: $6.3 billion Binance hack likely work of North Korea, experts say
keyFacts: Crypto industry analysts said hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest cyber heist ever.
The FBI and TRM Labs attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit.
Binance said it will cover all customer losses and expects to resume suspended withdrawals within two days.
body: A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm said a cyber unit was likely behind an attack that stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

Binance said on Friday that deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals were suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two. The company, which worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets, also said it will cover all customer losses.
In a social media post, Binance said that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, while a subsequent probe uncovered additional "points of breach."
Crypto industry analysts say the hack against Binance is the largest cyber heist ever.
What is TraderTraitor?

In a post on its website Thursday, tech security firm TRM Labs attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea's elite hacking unit. "We make this judgment with high confidence," TRM said.

"An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," the firm said. That would make the hack the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, it said.
The FBI on Saturday also accused TraderTraitor of being behind the attack, saying the hackers have been converting the stolen funds into Ethereum, a popular cryptocurrency.
The hackers are preparing the funds for "further laundering stages," the FBI said in a statement.
In 2025, TraderTraitor also targeted another crypto exchange, Bybit, in an attack resulting in a $1.5 billion loss, according to the FBI.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack," TRM said.
Jonathan Levin, co-founder and CEO of blockchain research firm Chainalysis, also said on social media that the Binance hack was "likely done" by TraderTraitor.

Analysts believe that TraderTraitor members are part of a wider North Korean hacking unit known as Lazarus Group, which targets multiple institutions across government, finance and other fields, according to the U.S. Treasury Department.
The Justice Department alleged in 2018 that the for an attack on Sony Pictures Entertainment four years earlier that leaked a massive amount of sensitive company data online.
Working "around the clock"

Binance said on social media that its "teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.

In December 2022, South Korea's spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen an estimated 1.5 trillion won ($1.1 billion) in cryptocurrency and other virtual assets in the past five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone. It said North Korea's capacity to steal digital assets was considered among the best in the world.

Changpeng Zhao, also known as CZ, founded Binance in 2017. In 2023, he pleaded guilty to a felony linked to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as the company's CEO. President Trump .

Zhao posted Thursday on social media that "User funds are safe!" but added that the theft "does look like a hack on Binance." He added that, while he no longer manages Binance, "As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."
The event, meanwhile, also raises questions about why stronger approval controls were not in place, said Kok Tin Gan, cofounder and CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab.

"This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet," he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users' "private keys," or unique authorizations, digitally and which are connected to the internet.
Binance said on social media it had "found no evidence of any wallet private key leak" and that the company would release more technical details when its probe is complete.

articles.headline: Andy Weir's New Time-Travel Sci-fi Thriller Officially Arrives Nov. 5
keyFacts: The new Audible Original time-travel thriller Exoplanet will launch exclusively on Nov. 5.
Author Benjamin Percy wrote the full-cast audio production, which is executive produced by Andy Weir.
Actors Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo star as a stranded starship crew.
body: Andy Weir is known for combining humor, hard science fiction, and gripping survival stories in his bestselling novels The Martian and Project Hail Mary, which were both adapted into blockbuster films. He’s sticking to that formula for his next project, a time-travel thriller that will launch on Audible on Nov. 5.

Weir is the executive producer for the new Audible Original Exoplanet, written by The Ninth Metal and Red Moon author Benjamin Percy. The full-cast immersive audio production stars Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo as the crew of a starship that is torn apart by a quantum anomaly. They all wind up on the same planet, but in different times, and have to try to help each other while being hunted by an alien intelligence seeking to use human technology to manipulate the future.

"I'm obsessed with problems, the kind where one person and a lot of math are all that stand between survival and disaster,” Weir said in a statement. “Benjamin Percy’s writing in Exoplanet takes that and adds a twist that genuinely kept me up at night: what if the people trying to save each other were separated not by distance, but by centuries? You can't see that story. You have to hear it. The crackle across a five-hundred-year gap, the desperation in a voice that doesn't know if anyone's still listening.”

While Weir hasn’t explored time travel in his books before, communication challenges are a recurring theme. The stranded astronaut Mark Watney has to use the Pathfinder probe to reach out to NASA and Project Hail Mary’s Wyland Grace records messages to send back to Earth along with samples of Taumoeba and has to wait years to learn if his mission was successful.

"Andy Weir’s stories transform rigorous science into big-hearted thrill rides with heart-stopping action and intense human emotion,” North America head of Audible content Marshall Lewy said in a statement. “That’s why Andy’s books have sold millions and inspired blockbuster films. With Andy as executive producer and Benjamin Percy crafting beautiful scripts specifically for the ear, Exoplanet is built for the audiences who loved Project Hail Mary and The Martian while also giving them something entirely new.”
Exoplanet launches exclusively on Audible on Nov. 5.

articles.headline: Canelo Álvarez defeats Christian Mbilli for WBC super-middleweight championship – live reaction
keyFacts: Canelo Alvarez defeated Christian Mbilli by a 12-round decision to capture the WBC super-middleweight championship in Riyadh.
Alvarez delivered a controlled performance in the second half of the fight, capitalizing on a point deduction for Mbilli in the eighth round.
In the undercard, Jaime Munguia retained his WBA super-middleweight title by a unanimous decision over Nikita Zon following a dramatic sixth round.
body: Álvarez, in a brief Spanish-language detour, references to the security situation in Saudi Arabia following the recent Houthi attacks, which have cast a shadow over tonight’s event in Riyadh.

También quiero agradecerle a mi familia, que me está viendo desde lejos hoy por primera vez. Muchas gracias a todos: a mis hermanos, a mis papás, a mis hijas, a mi hijo, a mi esposa, que no pudo venir tampoco por circunstancias. Pero muchas gracias. Los amo mucho.

I also want to thank my family, who are watching me from afar today for the first time. Thank you all so much: my siblings, my parents, my daughters, my son, and my wife – who also couldn’t make it due to certain circumstances. But thank you all so much. I love you very much.

Álvarez did not elaborate on the circumstances, but his remarks offered a rare acknowledgment of the extraordinary backdrop to a fight that went ahead despite deadly attacks on the Saudi capital in recent weeks.

For a fighter who has spent most of his adult life stacking championship belts across four weight classes, the experience of going without one appears to have weighed heavily on Canelo Álvarez. The 36-year-old Mexican was visibly emotional after reclaiming the WBC super-middleweight title, struggling to put into words what the moment meant to him.

“Oh, it’s so difficult to explain. It’s so difficult to explain,” Álvarez said in his rapidly improving English, surrounded by members of his team. “It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title. Now, after 20, 21 years as a professional – 16 years ago, I won my first title. Now I won the title again.”

Álvarez, who lost his undisputed championship to Terence Crawford 13 months ago in Las Vegas, had entered Saturday’s contest as a challenger for the first time since 2022. His performance suggested a fighter with something to prove, particularly over the second half of the contest, when his crisp counterpunching and deft footwork increasingly frustrated the younger champion.
“I’m so proud, so proud of my team,” Álvarez said. “Eddy Reynoso, Chepo Reynoso, who made me who I am, who made me the champion I am. Thank you so much for everything, Eddy. Thank you so much.”
Álvarez also thanked his family back home, with the interviewer relaying a joke that his wife had warned him not to return without the championship belt.
“I won that title!” Álvarez replied.
Asked whether he would have done anything differently over the 12 rounds, the newly crowned champion offered a characteristically succinct assessment.

No surprises here.Canelo Álvarez has won a 12-round decision over Christian Mbilli to capture the WBC super-middleweight title. The official scores were 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. (The Guardian had it 117-110).

Mbilli surely needs a knockout to retain his title, yet the urgency is nowhere to be seen. Álvarez is practically inviting the champion to come forward, but the Frenchman remains oddly hesitant to engage. It’s a baffling finish from a fighter whose reputation was built on relentless pressure. Álvarez will be a three-time super-middleweight champion as soon as these scores are tallied ...

More of the same. Álvarez in total control. Says Stephen “Breadman” Edwards, the respected Philadelphia-based boxing trainer: “Mbilli is lucky this is not the Canelo of 2018-21. He would’ve been stopped already. Mbilli is not performing well [in my opinion]. He’s outthinking himself.”

Another assured round from Álvarez, whose jab is sharp, his counters precise and his movement economical, stepping out of range whenever Mbilli tries to mount an attack. It’s a masterclass in ring generalship from the wily vet, who appears to have his French foe completely figured out. Canelo enters the championship rounds with an yawning advantage on our card.

Mbilli is playing straight into Álvarez’s hands. The relentless pressure and workrate has all but vanished, allowing the 36-year-old Mexican to fight at his own pace. He’s stacking rounds now and it’s hard to see how the Frenchman can turn it around.

A spot of controversy in the eighth as Mbilli is docked a point for punching behind the head following complaints from Álvarez, who appears to have the referee’s ear. The Mexican is then granted another timeout, further disrupting the champion’s rhythm. Mbilli needs to become more assertive, but Hector Afu’s officiating is now bound to become a talking point in a fight that remains very much in the balance.

Here comes Canelo. The Mexican produces his best round of the fight, looking increasingly comfortable as his heavier, more eye-catching counters begin to take their toll. A crisp combination off the ropes, punctuated by a flush right uppercut that rocks Mbilli, leaves no doubt.

Mbilli takes the initiative, putting together combinations and keeping Álvarez occupied with a steady stream of punches. Both men find openings to the midsection, but neither has really shifted into top gear. It’s a tactical, closely contested fight so far, with the Frenchman’s greater activity giving him the edge on our card.

Another competitive round with Mbilli increasing his output and doing some good work to the body while Álvarez grows a little too comfortable on the defensive. Canelo is slipping punches and looking to land the occasional big counter, but he’s not throwing enough. Mbilli finishes strongly, his speed and volume beginning to pose serious questions for the Mexican. Álvarez shades it on our card, but the champion is making him work for everything.

Mbilli is finding his rhythm now, ripping off combinations and using his superior workrate to back Álvarez against the ropes. Canelo is showing his age at times, but his lead hand looks as sharp as it has in years and his footwork remains crisp as he repeatedly pirouettes out of danger. It’s an intriguing contrast in styles: Mbilli has the advantage in volume, while Álvarez is landing the cleaner, more accurate punches and doing his best to dictate the pace. Another close round.

Mbilli is throwing and landing more and appears to have found his footing after a slow start. Álvarez is mostly picking his spots and pot-shotting. This one could have gone either way but it says here the champion nicked it.

Álvarez holds his ground in the center of the ring early before circling Mbilli, looking the sharper and more composed fighter. The Mexican puts together a couple of crisp combinations, including a thudding left hook, while Mbilli is slow to get going. The Frenchman finally begins letting his hands go in the final 30 seconds, but he’ll need to increase his volume to trouble Canelo. CompuBox has Álvarez landing 10 of 24 punches to Mbilli’s seven of 43. A clear opening round for the challenger.
The waiting is over. The final instructions have been given by referee Hector Afu, the seconds are out and we’ll pick it up with round-by-round coverage from here!

Here come the fighters. First it’s Mbilli, entering first despite his status as the champion, wearing a black tee and red trunks. And now after an extended video introduction it’s time for Canelo. It’s a muted, pyrotechnic-free ringwalk by his theatrical standards as he enters surrounded by his team and the recording artist Tito Double P.

Anthem time at Kingdom Arena. First the national anthem of Saudi Arabia, in honor of our hosts. Then La Marseillaise, for Mbilli. Then Himno Nacional Mexicano, for Canelo. The fighters should be making their entrances any moment now.
Munguía, speaking through a translator, is candid about his struggles in the sixth round, admitting he got carried away after hurting Zon and left himself exposed.

Pues la verdad que me agarró, o sea, me agarró tirando golpes, lo agarré y me fui con todo. Entonces descuide descuidé y fue cuando me agarró este. Pues digo, es parte del trabajo, pero hay que aprender. Y hay que, pues, aprender a no descuidarnos.

Well, honestly, he caught me. I mean, he caught me while I was throwing punches. I caught him too, and I went all out. So I let my guard down, and that’s when he caught me. Like I said, it’s part of the job, but you have to learn from it. You have to learn not to let your guard down.
The Mexican gave himself a six or seven out of 10 for his performance.

No la la verdad que me siento muy bien. Muy contento. Honrado. Este contento para el trabajo. El desempeño este. Yo creo que digo se me complicó ahí un poquito en rival. Pero la verdad que me me siento muy bien. Casi ellos pudimos sacar el trabajo. Y yo creo que es parte del aprendizaje. Y hay que seguir trabajando mucho.

Honestly, I feel really good. Very happy. Honored. I’m pleased with the work – with the performance. Things got a bit complicated with the opponent, but, truly, I feel very good. We managed to get the job done, and I think it’s all part of the learning process. We just have to keep working hard.
Munguía has retained his WBA super-middleweight title by a 12-round unanimous decision. The three judges at ringside handed down scores of 116-112 and 117-111 (twice).

The 30-year-old Mexican entered the ring as roughly an 18-1 favorite with the bookmakers. Zon nearly made a mockery of those odds, coming within a whisker of stopping the Mexican champion in an extraordinary sixth round, but Munguía was dominant throughout the second half of the contest to wrap up a close but uncontroversial win.

We may have just witnessed the round of the year in Riyadh. Nikita Zon had Jaime Munguía on the brink of defeat in a white-knuckle sixth, rocking the Mexican champion with a barrage of punches that left him barely able to stay upright. But Munguía somehow weathered the storm and came roaring back, hurting a punched-out Zon in the closing stages as the two traded hellfire in a remarkable display of courage and violence.

There was controversy, too, when referee Tony Weeks stepped between the fighters as Munguía appeared close to being stopped, giving the champion precious seconds to recover. The intervention could prove decisive.
The numbers tell part of the story: Zon landed 28 of 65 punches to Munguía’s 18 of 54, with 43 of their combined 46 connections coming on power shots. An unforgettable three minutes.
Jaime Munguía is (finally) in the ring for the final preliminary bout of the night, defending his World Boxing Association super-middleweight title against unbeaten Russian challenger Nikita Zon.

The 30-year-old Mexican (46-2, 35 KOs) claimed the belt with a unanimous-decision victory over Armando Resendiz in May and now makes his first defense against Zon (12-0-1, 10 KOs), who is fighting outside his native Russia for the first time.

Munguía, who lost to Canelo Álvarez by unanimous decision in May 2024, will be looking to make a statement ahead of his compatriot’s appearance in the main event. The winner could move into position for a 168lb unification fight with whoever emerges victorious between Álvarez and Christian Mbilli later tonight.

While we wait (and wait, and wait) for the final undercard bout, a few choice quotes from Thursday’s final press conference in Riyadh, where Álvarez and Mbilli struck contrasting notes ahead of tonight’s WBC super-middleweight title fight.
For Álvarez, who is for the first time since 2022 after losing his undisputed championship to Terence Crawford last year, the message was one of unfinished business.
“After 20 years as a professional, I’m glad to be here,” the 36-year-old Mexican said. “I’m the challenger now, but always in my mind, I’m the champion.”
He added: “I don’t believe in shortcuts. I’m going straight for the champion because I already have the experience. I’ve been a champion for many years and I want to be a champion again.”
Mbilli, the unbeaten Cameroon-born Frenchman making his first defense of the full WBC title, was no less confident.

“I’m ready for this fight. I’m ready to shock the world,” the 31-year-old said. “I have a lot of respect for Canelo and I want to congratulate him, but on Saturday it’s going to be a different story. I’m coming for the win.”
Asked about his preparations, Mbilli offered a simple formula: “My training camp was perfect. My mind is ready for this fight. I don’t need to do anything special to win; I only need to be myself.”

The undercard is nearing its conclusion as we build towards tonight’s main event between Álvarez and Mbilli, with one preliminary bout remaining before the headliners make their ringwalks. Jaime Munguía is up next to defend his WBA super-middleweight title against Nikita Zon in a scheduled 12-round contest.

In the most recent bout, Rafael Espinoza retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO of Ricardo Blandon, who was unable to continue after suffering a cut caused by a punch. The unbeaten Mexican improved to 29-0 with 25 knockouts. It should be noted the stoppage felt awfully premature.
Earlier, Japan’s Reito Tsutsumi overwhelmed Raymundo Rojas with a series of heavy left hands to force a second-round stoppage at 2min 27sec, improving his professional record to 6-0.

On the non-televised card, Brayan Leon outpointed Hector Aguirre over eight rounds, while Emiliano Rojo stopped Flavius Biea in the fourth. Bek Nurmaganbet needed less than three minutes to dispatch Marcos Vazquez, dropping him twice before securing a first-round knockout with just three seconds to go.
Before that, Sultan Almohammed earned a unanimous decision over Erick Villegas, while Carl Jammes Martin edged David Picasso by split decision in a closely contested featherweight contest.

Hello and welcome Riyadh’s Kingdom Arena for tonight’s fight between Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez and Christian Mbilli from Riyadh, where one of boxing’s biggest names is attempting to reclaim his place atop the super-middleweight division in circumstances that are anything but ordinary.

For the first time since 2022, Álvarez enters the ring as a challenger. The 36-year-old Mexican superstar, who lost his undisputed championship to Terence Crawford 13 months ago, is seeking to regain the World Boxing Council title against the unbeaten, Cameroon-born Frenchman Mbilli, who has promised to “shock the world” in the biggest fight of his career.

But the backdrop is almost as compelling as the matchup itself. The contest is going ahead despite a wave of drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia that have forced the cancellation or postponement of other major events and raised questions about whether the fight could safely take place. After weeks of uncertainty, the fighters are here, the stage is set and the show, remarkably, goes on.
Stay with us for all the buildup, round-by-round coverage and reaction from Riyadh.

articles.headline: Canelo Alvarez outclasses Christian Mbilli to claim WBC title and put Terence Crawford demons to bed
keyFacts: Canelo Alvarez secured a unanimous decision victory over Christian Mbilli to reclaim the WBC super middleweight crown in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Judges scored the bout 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 in favor of Alvarez.
Alvarez stated he plans to take a couple of weeks off before returning to the ring in February.
body: Canelo Alvarez got an answer to the question that had haunted him ever since his lopsided defeat to Terence Crawford last September.

On Halloween in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Canelo proved that there is still life in the old dog, as he secured a comfortable unanimous decision victory over Christian Mbilli to reclaim the WBC super middleweight crown.
Canelo Alvarez rolled back the years to outpoint Christian Mbilli on Saturday night
Canelo methodically picked apart defending champion Mbilli, who got off to a strong start before letting the fight slip away from him in the middle portion of the fight.
Mbilli looked overawed by the occasion, while Canelo showed flashes of his former self.
In portions, he rolled back the years with some beautiful counters, and in the end, he was the deserved winner.
All three judges sided with the future first-ballot Hall of Famer by margins of 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110.
“It’s so difficult to explain; it feels unbelievable,” an emotional Canelo said after reclaiming one of the pieces of the undisputed puzzle he dropped to Crawford.
“This feels like my first world title. 16 years ago I won my first world title as a professional.
“Now I win the world title again, and I’m so proud and so proud of my team.
“Eddy Reynoso (Trainer and manager) made me the man I am. Thank you so much, Eddy.”
Canelo is now expected to return to the ring in February for what will be the fourth and final fight of his money-spinning $180m deal with Riyadh Season.
Two of his potential next dance partners, Lester Martinez and Hamzah Sheeraz, were ringside in the Saudi capital.
Canelo reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title, one of the four belts he dropped to Crawford last September
But Canelo stopped short of calling for a name when he was asked what would come next.
“I’m going to rest,” added Canelo. “I’m going to keep learning.
“I am going to keep working hard. I will take a couple of weeks off, and then I will be back.”

articles.headline: Anthropic hiring manager says he stopped giving coding interviews because Claude is better at them — and tells junior engineers that 'hunger beats tenure'
keyFacts: Anthropic engineering manager Felix Rieseberg announced in a blog post that he has stopped giving traditional coding interviews.
Rieseberg stated that the decision was made because the Claude AI model can code better than human candidates.
Rieseberg is currently examining new ways to evaluate candidates who build well with artificial intelligence.
body: - Anthropic hiring manager Felix Rieseberg reveals that coding interviews are over
- In a blog post, the engineering manager explains that Claude codes better, making coding tasks obsolete
- Rieseberg encourages junior engineers to approach their work with a new attitude, while he examines a way to interview people who are good at AI coding
The end is nigh for coding tasks in interviews, certainly as far as Anthropic is concerned.

The AI company’s engineering manager Felix Rieseberg has published a blog post explaining how junior engineers should approach jobs and their current roles, after announcing the abandonment of coding interviews.

His rationale for the decision is straightforward: AI codes better than humans, making the assessment pretty pointless. At a time when Claude can demonstrate a superior grasp of coding, putting job candidates through the process no longer reveals anything “meaningful about the candidates,” according to Rieseberg.
Instead, he advises that junior engineers should focus instead on making an impact, while taking the time to understand the company and the people working within it.
No code candidates
Rieseberg is quick to the point: “This month, I laid the traditional coding interview to rest. As a hiring manager at Anthropic, I stopped asking candidates to do them.”

He explains that while coding challenges in interviews were once useful, that is no longer the past. “There’s no more point in giving you a little React challenge than there is in quizzing people about assembly; Claude is now better at both.”

Instead, Rieseberg offers some anecdotes of people who were active agents of change when joining new companies, and suggests making an impact is the answer. Radical ideas and a weekend coding a prototype with AI are the new coding interview, essentially, approaching being hired with a demonstration of the project they prompted and finessed, and its outcome.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Sheer ignorance”

Rieseberg’s decision may have come out of the blue, but his rationale seems to make some sort of sense. He quotes actor and director Orson Welles, who responded to a question about his confidence to try new things with “Ignorance, sheer ignorance — you know there’s no confidence to equal it. It’s only when you know something about a profession, I think, that you’re timid or careful.”

With that as context, Rieseberg’s conclusion that coding interviews are not the answer when the company product already codes better than anyone it can hire has legs. Perhaps it was inevitable that the day would come, but crucially, Rieseberg isn’t giving up on hiring. Instead, he’s looking for a new way to do it, a route to finding new junior engineers without them needing a coding assessment.

“I’m probably not the only manager trying to figure out how to interview for people who build well with AI. I haven’t quite gotten there yet — but I’m scanning resumes and portfolios for little prototypes that exhibit taste, empathy, and principled thinking.”

articles.headline: The Slate vs Ford Fathom debate might be settled by this one key tech feature
keyFacts: Ford and Slate are developing electric pickup trucks priced below $30,000 using different approaches to cabin technology.
Ford said the Fathom will feature a built-in touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus a digital key.
Slate relies on the user's phone or tablet for infotainment instead of including a traditional dashboard display.
body: The Slate vs Ford Fathom debate might be settled by this one key tech feature
Ford keeps CarPlay and Android Auto in its affordable EV truck, while Slate expects you to bring the screen yourself.

Both Ford and Slate are pursuing the same enticing goal: an electric pickup starting below $30,000. The Blank Slate Truck starts at $24,950 plus a $1,450 destination charge, while the Ford Fathom starts at $28,350 plus a $1,595 destination charge.

But things get more interesting once you look more closely. Ford says the Fathom will feature a large touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Slate forgoes a traditional infotainment system, instead giving you a place to mount and charge your phone. That's refreshingly simple for some, but it might seem too simple for anyone used to seeing maps, music and messages on a proper center display.
Slate makes your phone the infotainment system

Slate hasn't merely left CarPlay off the options sheet. Its approach is to have your phone or tablet do the work. Phone mounting and charging are standard, and buyers can opt for accessory speakers and a bracket that fits a larger tablet. Navigation, music and other compatible apps normally accessed through CarPlay or Android Auto remain on the device. Slate told InsideEVs that vehicle software updates can be downloaded onto a phone and transferred to the truck, avoiding the need for an embedded cellular connection.

There's a certain logic to it: if the infotainment hardware is in your pocket, it can't get hopelessly dated as the truck ages. There are compromises, however. A phone screen is smaller than a dedicated dashboard display. And although Slate left out the infotainment screen to keep things simple, some prospective owners online are already discussing aftermarket stereos, Raspberry Pi projects and other ways to get CarPlay or Android Auto into the truck.

Ford takes the more familiar route. The Fathom's built-in display will support CarPlay and Android Auto, and the truck will also get a digital key, bidirectional power and hardware for Ford's next-generation BlueCruise hands-free system — which requires activation. Ford hasn't yet announced the Fathom's projected range, towing capacity or payload. Preorders begin in early 2027.
Ford and Slate are cutting costs in very different places
That infotainment gap makes more sense when you consider how these companies are building a cheap EV.

Slate is starting from scratch, so it is ruthlessly questioning what needs to be included. Ford has been making vehicles for more than a century and its answer is to simplify engineering and assembly while keeping more familiar equipment in the cabin.

Ford is investing $2 billion to retool Louisville Assembly Plant around its Universal EV Production System. The automaker says the platform uses 20 percent fewer parts than a typical vehicle, 50 percent fewer cooling hoses and connections and a wiring harness more than 4,000 feet shorter than the one in its first-generation electric SUV, the Mustang Mach-E. Assembly is expected to net out at 15 percent faster than the plant's previous products. It's a lot of engineering aimed at cutting manufacturing costs without making the cabin look unfinished.

Smartphone integration isn't an afterthought for buyers. Deloitte's 2025 Global Automotive Consumer Study surveyed over 31,000 consumers in 30 countries and found that 63 percent of US respondents considered smartphone connectivity via CarPlay or Android Auto in their next vehicle somewhat or very important.

Slate's approach isn't necessarily wrong. A less expensive, two-door electric pickup with fewer electronics may be just what some buyers want. CarPlay or Android Auto could be one of those little features that feel much bigger after you've lived without them. The five-seat Fathom, meanwhile, is shaping up as a more conventional daily driver.

articles.headline: Attorneys for Alaska say ‘meritless’ Trump demand to set aside Senate ballots ‘not even possible’
keyFacts: Alaska's state government urged a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit seeking to stop certification of the state's U.S. Senate race, officials said.
The lawsuit alleges voter confusion over a second Dan Sullivan, but state officials called demands to separate those ballots disturbing and impossible.
U.S. District Court Judge Sharon L. Gleason set a Saturday deadline for arguments regarding whether to dismiss the lawsuit without a hearing.
body: ANCHORAGE, Alaska (AP) — Alaska’s Republican-run state government on Saturday urged a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed at President Donald Trump’s direction to stop the certification of a possible Democratic win in that state’s pivotal U.S. Senate race, writing that there is “no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer.”

The scathing filing from the state’s attorney general’s office comes as U.S. District Court Judge Sharon L. Gleason set a deadline of Saturday for arguments over whether she should dismiss the lawsuit without even a hearing. The complaint from the U.S. Department of Justice has been roundly criticized by election law experts and demands that the judge halt certification of a possible win by Democrat Mary Peltola until it is determined whether voters were confused by the presence of a second candidate on the ballot with the same name as her main rival, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

The Department of Justice on Friday added a request that the judge separate all ballots showing votes for the second Dan Sullivan until it can be determined whether voters were fooled into wasting their votes for a spoiler candidate. In its Saturday filing, Alaska said this was “both disturbing and impossible.” It added there would be no way to do that without violating voter privacy.

Trump also demanded that Peltola be prosecuted after The New York Times this week reported that internal texts and posts appear to show the Democrats’ campaign was involved in recruiting the second Sullivan, a retired school teacher in the remote fishing village of Petersburg, onto the ballot. But the state filing notes that the two Sullivans are distinguished from each other on the ballot — the senator is listed as a Republican and the incumbent, while the other simply as “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.”

“State officials carefully designed the ballot to minimize voter confusion,” Alaska officials wrote. “The Court should immediately dismiss this lawsuit with prejudice and allow state officials to conduct the general election — including ballot counting and certification — free from unwarranted federal interference.”

The Trump administration argued that a preamble to the 1990s law governing voter registration gave it the responsibility for ensuring states maintained the “integrity” of federal elections. It has said it’s simply trying to combat fraud by preventing the Democrat from being declared the victor in a race that could determine which party controls the U.S. Senate.

The Department of Justice issued a wave of subpoenas and announced it was conducting a criminal investigation in the case as the administration has stepped up its use of its legal powers to support Trump’s side in the midterm election .

Peltola has denied involvement in the presence of the second Sullivan on the ballot. The Times report was based on interviews with her former campaign manager, texts and contributions from a political group backing Peltola to an out-of-state Democratic consultant who recruited the second Sullivan.

Alaska’s Republican governor, Mike Dunleavy, who announced a state probe into the situation after the Times story, has condemned the placement of the second Sullivan on the ballot. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled this summer that the second candidate fulfilled all legal requirements to stay on. The state government’s filing on Saturday says that the new revelations about the possible role of Peltola’s campaign don’t change the fact that he’s legally on the ballot.
“Not every wrong can be righted in federal court,” the state wrote.
Peltola’s campaign and voting rights groups also have urged Gleason to dismiss the case, putting them in unusual alignment with Alaska state officials.

“Imagine if the federal executive could pluck a few words like ‘election integrity’ from some statutory preamble and, on that basis alone, bend the machinery of state elections to his will, preemptively blocking certification of a U.S. Senate election to protect his preferred candidate from defeat and then subjecting voters to a law-enforcement-led inquest about who they ‘really’ supported,” the American Civil Liberties Union wrote in a filing urging the lawsuit’s dismissal. “Imagine that world and ask whether it is what the Framers wanted or precisely what they most feared.”

articles.headline: Dutch authorities rescue 38 people adrift in rubber boat
keyFacts: Dutch authorities rescued 38 men found adrift in a motorless rubber boat off the Dutch coast.
Military police spokesperson Doron Wallin said 36 men are from Afghanistan and two suspected smugglers are from Sudan.
Dutch authorities will open an investigation into the case on Sunday.
body: Authorities in the Netherlands have rescued 38 people found adrift in a rubber boat off the Dutch coast, in one of the first such interceptions for the country.

Two of the people on board the dinghy when it was rescued are thought to be smugglers, while the rest are migrants, military police spokesperson Doron Wallin told The Associated Press news agency on Saturday.
“We don’t know where they came from – France, the Netherlands or Belgium – and we don’t know where the boat was heading,” Wallin said.
The boat was discovered drifting with no motor off the coast of the Netherlands’ Zeeland province, far southwest of Amsterdam. No one was wearing a life vest.

All 38 on the boat were men, 36 of whom were from Afghanistan, and two – the suspected smugglers – were from Sudan, according to the AFP news agency. The two Sudanese men have been arrested on suspicion of people smuggling.

It is not known where the boat was headed, but refugee and migrant crossings in small boats from France to the United Kingdom have become commonplace in recent years. It is unusual for boats to be discovered in Dutch waters, however.
“These are things you usually see in France and Belgium. We rarely see it here in the Netherlands before today,” Wallin said.
Dutch authorities will open an investigation into the case on Sunday.

body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth’s father weighed in on the Michigan Senate race on Friday by going after Democratic nominee Abdul el Sayed .
While speaking on comedian Hasan Minhaj’s podcast earlier in the week, el Sayed discussed a topic that’s come up often throughout his campaign against Republican rival Mike Rogers: sports.
But instead of taking aim at Rogers, el Sayed conjectured about how Hegseth’s parents treated their son’s athletic life differently than his did.

“Pete Hegseth, everybody knows that guy from the locker room. He would have rode the pine,” el Sayed said, using an idiom referring to sitting on the bench. “He probably got to start two games his entire career playing whatever sport it was, and his parents came and cheered so hard for him. And as a kid whose parents never came, right, and started every game, part of me is just like, bro, I feel bad for you, somebody told you you were a lot better than you really are.”
Sports has emerged as a key theme throughout the Michigan Senate race, largely due to both Rogers and el Sayed claiming past athletic prowess.

El Sayed served as the captain of his high school football team and played club lacrosse at the University of Michigan, while Rogers also played high school football and is the son of a football coach. Rogers has highlighted this theme in advertisements and knocked el Sayed for a 2021 essay he wrote in which he referenced football in the context of “toxic masculinity.”

Hegseth’s father, Brian Hegseth, jumped into the fray by saying el Sayed suffers from “little man syndrome” and he “has no idea what he’s talking about.” Hegseth played basketball at Princeton University.

“Proud to say, as Pete’s dad, he was an absolute star on the court in HS. Captain, all-conference, all-state player… earned!” he said. “We parents have cheered him on, yes. That’s what families do–support each other. #Envy makes him bitter.”

articles.headline: Anthropic Blocks AI Game Clones in Claude Opus Update
keyFacts: Anthropic updated Claude Opus 5.5 to block the generation of specific existing game recreations in order to prevent intellectual property infringement.
The update follows complaints from players and developers about low-effort AI-generated game clones flooding platforms like Steam.
Anthropic staff member Addy Osmani stated that original games and assets will continue to work while the company iterates on the policy.
body: Anthropic has issued an update for Claude that puts a stop to the AI-generated game clones that have filled platforms like Steam.

The term 'AI slop' is something we've heard a lot in the past few years, but it became especially prevalent in the gaming community after Valve launched Steam Next Fest earlier this month. PC users quickly launched complaints that their feeds had been filled with low-effort clones not only of pre-existing games but even some titles that had only just released their own demos.

As players trudged through the slop, developers faced a reality that threw months or even years of hard work into jeopardy. Some, including Drunken Goddess Reflux developer Alliance Arts and Who You , even took action by canceling their Steam demo plans in favor of private playtests. It's a situation that rapidly spun out of control, prompting a response from Valve itself as it said it would be "thinking about how to solve this problem."
ANTHROPIC IS CRACKING DOWN ON VIDEO GAME REWRITES 🚨
Claude Code picked up a new rule around Oct 27, sent from Anthropic’s servers under a flag called "tengu_heron_brook". There’s no setting to turn it off.

The full rule: “Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.”
Is this the end of game rewrites, modding and everything in between?
— chasm (@chasmmmmmmmmmmm) October 30, 2026

As reported by Game Developer , X/Twitter user Chasm was one of the first to share evidence of tech company Anthropic taking action against video game copycats. Based on their findings, Claude, the company's AI assistant, recently received an update featuring a new rule. The full rule can be read below:
"Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original."
When reached for comment by Game Developer, Anthropic pointed to a post shared by Addy Osmani, a member of its technical staff. Osmani's explanation can be read below:

"We added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else's specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy. Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working. We'll continue to iterate to ensure we're striking the right balance. In the meantime, if Claude turns down something that's yours, send it my way."
Whether there was a specific event or reason that prompted Anthropic to make these changes is unclear.

Game developers and game enjoyers will no doubt find comfort in Anthropic's changes, though it's worth noting that how impactful any of this will be remains to be seen. At the very least, those who use Claude to rip ideas directly from those who used their minds and time to bring them to life should have a tougher time trying to profit off of the work of others.

The industry is struggling to come to grips with artificial intelligence. Some, such as Epic Games' Tim Sweeney, have insisted that Valve should stray from asking developers to disclose games utilizing generative AI materials . Others, including Super Smash Bros. mastermind Masahiro Sakurai, have compared AI-generated games to "low-quality goods." The developers behind VRChat, meanwhile, recently came under fire for how they are handling AI content .

articles.headline: Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
keyFacts: Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company's position in the artificial intelligence landscape during a recent interview with Wired.

body: During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy, Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape.

Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer. But while Ternus — a longtime Apple executive who officially became CEO at the beginning of September — acknowledged that “everyone has an opinion,” he insisted, “I really like where we’re at.”

Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”

And when Levy pressed him on whether AI might affect Apple and its ecosystem more dramatically, with agents potentially making things like apps unnecessary, Ternus replied,”That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do.”

articles.headline: FromSoftware temporarily shuts down Dark Souls 2 and 3 multiplayer over 'server issue'

body: As reported by Eurogamer, FromSoftware has shut down multiplayer (invasions, co-op, messages) in Dark Souls 2 and 3 for an indeterminate amount of time due to an undisclosed "server issue." The company shared the news in an October 30 post on X, "The Everything App."

The closure affects all platforms for each respective game, and the company said that it would provide an updated timeline for server restoration once it had more information. This isn't the first time something like this has happened with FromSoftware's back catalogue. In early 2022, on the eve of Elden Ring's release, a catastrophic remote code execution vulnerability was discovered in all of the Dark Souls games. That resulted in PC servers for the series getting shut down for months.

But there are key differences here: It's only Dark Souls 2 and 3 this time around, while the issue extends to all platforms, not just PC. That gives me some hope that this issue is not only less serious, but it will take less time to resolve as well.

It honestly couldn't have happened at a better time for PC players, though: Legend modder Yui's Seamless co-op series runs on its own servers, separate from the official FromSoft ones, meaning the party's still going if you download the mod and play that way. Dark Souls 2 finally got the Seamless co-op treatment at the end of September (Dark Souls 3 has been covered for awhile).

As its name implies, Seamless Co-op makes it easier to play through the entirety of these games together with a friend or friends, offering shared progress and no disconnects on death or defeat of a boss. articles.headline: How House Democrats' 'deterrence message' on Trump jobs could backfire
keyFacts: Senator Elissa Slotkin stated she wants Democrats to pursue cases against Trump administration officials to deter young Americans from working for them.
Former federal prosecutor Abhishek Kambli warned that Slotkin's remarks could provide Trump officials with legal ammunition to challenge future congressional subpoenas.
Law professor Michael Morley questioned whether politicians' partisan motivations would ultimately serve as a valid basis for courts to invalidate subpoenas.
body: Sen. Elissa Slotkin's warning to young Americans not to join the Trump administration could backfire by handing Trump officials legal ammunition to derail the investigations Democrats hope to launch if they retake Congress, a former federal prosecutor warned.

The freshman Michigan Democrat said last month that she wants her party to pursue "signature cases" against officials who helped Trump, reasoning that it would discourage young Americans from considering jobs in his administration.

"I want that deterrence message sent," Slotkin said during an Oct. 13 event at the University of Chicago, describing how young graduates might fear "buying myself a ton of problems" by joining the administration.

But Abhishek Kambli, a former deputy associate attorney general in Trump's Justice Department , said Slotkin's remarks could backfire if Democrats retake either chamber of Congress in the midterm elections and gain greater control over congressional investigations.

"If they just throw in boilerplate language that this is for legislative purpose, anyone challenging those subpoenas will have that entire record to demonstrate that it's anything but that," Kambli, a partner at Holtzman Vogel, told Fox News Digital.
HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY

While Congress has broad authority to conduct investigations, subpoena witnesses and review government operations, the Supreme Court has ruled that lawmakers cannot use those powers solely to punish individuals.
The Supreme Court confronted those limits in 2020, when House Democrats attempted to obtain Trump's personal financial records through congressional subpoenas.

In Trump v. Mazars, the justices established a four-factor test requiring courts to examine whether Congress demonstrated a legitimate legislative need for the records, whether its requests were sufficiently narrow, whether the information could be obtained elsewhere and what burden the subpoenas would impose on the president.
The court sent the dispute back to lower courts without ruling that the subpoenas satisfied those standards, leaving unresolved questions about how the framework would be applied.

"So it's not enough just to tack on a legislative purpose," Kambli said, arguing that courts must look beyond Congress' stated reasons for an investigation to determine whether its demands are constitutionally justified.
Democrats' public remarks could become evidence against them if future subpoenas are challenged, according to Kambli.
SLOTKIN WANTS GOP PROSECUTIONS TO DETER YOUNG PEOPLE FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION JOBS

"They don't have to bury their head in the sand," Kambli said of the courts. "I think they have to look at the facts of the case and look at it in terms of how they fits into the broader comments that they made."

House Democrats are already laying the groundwork for investigations into Trump's family business dealings and potential conflicts of interest if they regain control of Congress. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., has also vowed to expand his investigation into donors funding Trump's White House ballroom if Democrats retake the Senate ,
But another constitutional law expert questioned whether Democrats' remarks would carry enough legal weight to undermine future congressional investigations.

Michael Morley, a professor at Florida State University College of Law, said courts generally recognize that politicians bring partisan motivations to congressional investigations and would be reluctant to invalidate subpoenas merely because of provocative public remarks.

"I don't think that the fact that there might be partisan motivations for a congressional investigation would ultimately be a valid basis for refusing to comply with a subpoena," Morley told Fox News Digital.

"At the end of the day, a court is going to be very reluctant to conclude, based on one or more members' possible subjective motivations, that Congress lacks constitutional authority to investigate," Morley said.
SLOTKIN'S VIRAL 'THREAT' TO CONSERVATIVES TAKES NEW TWIST AS STUDENT MOVES TO HOLD HER ACCOUNTABLE: 'SHOCKING'

He also emphasized that Trump v. Mazars focused specifically on subpoenas for the president's personal records, arguing that applying the same heightened legal standards to subpoenas targeting other administration officials would be a stretch.
But Morley said Slotkin's language could give judges pause when the legal basis for a subpoena is already uncertain.
"It's bad atmospherics," he said, adding that such statements could make courts "marginally less likely" to resolve doubts in Democrats' favor.

Slotkin has rejected accusations that she wants to target Americans merely for working for Republicans. She told CNN that she was talking about officials who break the law or misuse taxpayer dollars, calling the criticism "manufactured outrage."

But Kambli warned the consequences could extend beyond whether Democratic subpoenas survive legal challenges , saying that investigations could inflict financial and reputational damage even without criminal charges.

"There is the idea that the process is the punishment, and there is no doubt that some members of Congress intend to use the process to bankrupt people that can't afford legal representation," Kambli said.

He also said that while Trump's Justice Department would be unlikely to prosecute administration officials over criminal contempt referrals from a Democratic-controlled Congress, that could change under a future Democratic administration.
Morley also criticized the prospect of intimidating young government employees who may lack the resources to defend themselves.
"That's just not how we want our political disputes to be handled," Morley said.

articles.headline: Trump ask to set aside ‘Decoy Dan’ Alaska Senate ballots ‘not even possible’: attorneys
keyFacts: Alaska attorneys urged a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed at President Donald Trump's direction to halt certification of a Senate race.
The lawsuit demanded that ballots showing votes for a second candidate named Dan Sullivan be separated to check for voter confusion.
Alaska state officials stated in a filing that separating the ballots is impossible without violating voter privacy.
body: Trump ask to set aside ‘Decoy Dan’ Alaska Senate ballots ‘not even possible’: attorneys
By
Associated Press
Published Oct. 31, 2026, 5:22 p.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Alaska’s Republican-run state government on Saturday urged a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed at President Donald Trump’s direction to stop the certification of a possible Democratic win in that state’s pivotal U.S. Senate race, writing that there is “no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer.”

The scathing filing from the state’s attorney general’s office comes as U.S. District Court Judge Sharon L. Gleason set a deadline of Saturday for arguments over whether she should dismiss the lawsuit without even a hearing.

The complaint from the U.S. Department of Justice has been roundly criticized by election law experts and demands that the judge halt certification of a possible win by Democrat Mary Peltola until it is determined whether voters were confused by the presence of a second candidate on the ballot with the same name as her main rival, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

The Department of Justice on Friday added a request that the judge separate all ballots showing votes for the second Dan Sullivan until it can be determined whether voters were fooled into wasting their votes for a spoiler candidate.
In its Saturday filing, Alaska said this was “both disturbing and impossible.” It added there would be no way to do that without violating voter privacy.

Trump also demanded that Peltola be prosecuted after The New York Times this week reported that internal texts and posts appear to show the Democrats’ campaign was involved in recruiting the second Sullivan, a retired school teacher in the remote fishing village of Petersburg, onto the ballot.
Here’s the latest on the ‘Decoy Dan’ scandal in the ongoing Alaska Senate race:

But the state filing notes that the two Sullivans are distinguished from each other on the ballot — the senator is listed as a Republican and the incumbent, while the other simply as “Daniel J. Sullivan.”

“State officials carefully designed the ballot to minimize voter confusion,” Alaska officials wrote. “The Court should immediately dismiss this lawsuit with prejudice and allow state officials to conduct the general election — including ballot counting and certification — free from unwarranted federal interference.”

articles.headline: Get in the spirit with these horrors from YouTube
keyFacts: The Verge published a curated selection of creepy and weird YouTube videos to close out the Halloween season.
The recommendations include short films like Cecelia Condit's Possibly in Michigan and David B Earle's abstract loopable video.
The article suggests using these videos, ranging from surreal art house shorts to cosmic horror, to celebrate Halloween.
body: Rather than recommend a single horror film or an unsettling album for our final installment of spooky season recs, I present you with a small selection of creepy, disturbing, and just plain weird videos from YouTube. There’s a little something for everyone here. Whether you’re a fan of surreal art house shorts, cosmic horror, or classic viral clips, you’re bound to find something below that will get you in the Halloween spirit.
Get in the spirit with these horrors from YouTube
Close out the Halloween season with these creepy, weird, and unsettling videos from YouTube.

This 1983 short film from Cecelia Condit found its audience over 30 years later when it was uploaded to YouTube and eventually found its way to Reddit. If you’ve ever wondered what a feminist musical about cannibals directed by David Lynch would be like, wonder no more. Possibly in Michigan is only 12 minutes long, but it has inspired hours of YouTube videos dedicated to analyzing its deeply unsettling imagery and meaning.

The line between horror and comedy is razor thin, and Homemade Gatorade expertly threads that line. It’s bizarre, uncomfortable, and uncanny. It blends stiff animation with heavily processed video to create something quite unique. I’m never sure if I should be laughing or squirming in terror with every turn this road trip short takes.

Big budget cosmic horror films often make the same mistake — they try to show too much. What makes Portrait of God work is it knows less is more. So much of its short runtime is spent staring into an empty abyss. Or is it empty…

Speaking of staring intently at nothing and wondering if you did actually see anything, Heck is the short that eventually was turned into the experimental horror Skinamarink. Personally, I love Skinamarink, but I understand it’s not for everyone. 100 minutes is a long time to be staring into staticky corners of a drab suburban home. Heck delivers the same tension-building quiet, but in a much more digestible 29 minutes.

There’s not much to say about this one-minute loopable short from David B Earle. It’s the sort of video that did gangbusters on early YouTube. It’s all abstract creepiness and nightmare-fuel visuals. If you want the full effect and need something to put on the TV at your Halloween party, put on this four-hour looped version.
No Halloween is complete without this banger from Nick Lutsko.

articles.headline: Gears Of War Should Have Killed Off Marcus Fenix Years Ago
keyFacts: Marcus Fenix should have died in Gears of War 4 to pass the torch to a new generation, according to a GameSpot opinion piece.
The author argues that keeping Fenix alive due to franchise popularity undermines his character arc and the impact of the story.
Future Gears of War games chose to focus on a prequel instead of exploring the consequences of major character deaths from later installments.
body: Gears of War is arguably the most masculine property in video games. A franchise founded on the idea of muscular, refrigerator-sized dudes tearing apart stinky underground monsters with badass chainsaws until they’re covered in bloody viscera was always destined to attract such a reputation, but this only makes the moments when it subverts our expectations all the more impactful. Instances of quiet within its post-apocalyptic world, or conversations shared between its main cast when everything seems lost, always hit the hardest.

Once you strip away the chainsaw bayonets, you’re left with a profound narrative of grief as Marcus Fenix tries to save a humanity that is already flirting with extinction. While all of his muscles and bravado might make the man seem infallible, Fenix is frequently tasked with the impossible--to save a human race that is constantly under the threat of annihilation. He’s doomed to fail, to eventually fall alongside his comrades until a new generation emerges to continue the fight. This makes perfect narrative sense, and would also give the iconic hero some much needed rest. So, what would happen if The Coalition actually went through with it and killed him?

Ever since I first laid eyes on Marcus Fenix as he explored the darkened streets of a fallen city to the melancholic beauty of "Mad World, " I have viewed him as a tragic character. He’s fighting an impossible war after being freed from unjustified imprisonment, and spends the entire original trilogy watching close friends succumb to their personal demons or fall to an enemy that shows no signs of slowing. Making the player feel doomed from the outset can be an incredibly powerful storytelling tool, so it’s no surprise that E-Day focuses so heavily on the world falling apart as a younger roster of heroes is forced to take action.

When you turn up to save the day amidst the rubble of Kalona, it’s often about picking up the pieces while walking over fresh corpses of thousands, where finding even two survivors is a reason to celebrate given the circumstances. Not once does Fenix entertain leaving innocent people behind, and you truly feel for him when retreat becomes the only option. Unfortunately, once the excellent opening act concludes, the campaign settles into a predictable routine that can’t help feeling middle-of-the-road.

This question has been on my mind for over a decade now, since the character arc of Fenix came to a natural conclusion in Gears of War 3 after the Locust are defeated and humanity is guaranteed a future. Our flawed hero might be stricken with grief by the sacrifices of Dom and his other comrades, but he remains surrounded by people who love and care about him in ways that can now be treasured in a world where survival is guaranteed. But thanks to this need to keep popular franchises alive and avoid disappointing legions of fans, Marcus Fenix has remained integral to Gears ever since.

While the details are cloudy all these years later, there was a time when Gears of War was potentially going to leave the planet of Sera behind in pursuit of pastures new. Speaking to Game Informer as part of a cover story back in 2016 , creative director Chuck Osieja claimed that The Coalition was originally thinking about taking Gears to a fresh planet with an all-new cast of characters who were only loosely connected to what came before. So long as Gears focuses on the machinations of conflict with satisfying combat and a worthwhile story, I can see it taking place anywhere, but without the stewardship of Epic Games it settled for the most predictable destination imaginable. Marcus Fenix has a son, the Locust comes back, and humanity once again finds itself on the backfoot. Turns out the original trilogy was for naught.

Gears of War 4 centered on a new trio of likeable characters--JD Fenix, Kait Diaz, and Del Walker--who were all raised in a world without the Locust threat, but still living beneath the thumb of an outdated militaristic society that refuses to leave old habits behind. It’s a more saturated and freeing world, but the very same darkness awaits beneath the surface. As for Marcus Fenix, he has secluded himself in the wilderness after the death of his wife and the trauma of perpetual conflict, resentful of a son who decided to join a military he has actively come to despise. The war may be over, but Marcus has little interest in returning to a world that refuses to learn from its mistakes.

This new trilogy would eventually shift focus away from the Fenix family and instead mostly on Kait and her strange connection to the new Locust threat, with Gears 5 offering a harsh and sudden player choice in the final act as you’re asked to save the life of either JD or Del. Whoever you don’t choose is murdered before your eyes, but since the trilogy was ditched, at least for now, for a prequel in E-Day, we never get to witness the repercussions. Even Marcus seems pretty unfazed by the death of his only son, when this could have been a killer moment for decades of anger, grief, and resentment to culminate in something meaningful. Instead it’s brushed aside and never mentioned again, joining Halo’s Reclaimer trilogy as stories ripe with potential that Xbox left behind because market relevance was more important.

Rather than outliving his son and watching a world he helped save once again fall to ruin, Marcus Fenix should have perished in Gears of War 4 as he passes the torch onto a new generation. Not mauled by a horde of Locust in gruesome fashion as a twisted joke, but giving his life to people he cares about while cementing an enduring hope that things are worth fighting for. Beginning his new character arc as a jaded old man deciding to shield himself from the realities of a world he helped save before reaching a position where he possesses renewed hope in the coming generation would fit the narrative themes while being brave enough to leave our own nostalgia behind. Even in the same universe, we shouldn’t be afraid to fall in love with new characters and new stories, and realise titans like Marcus Fenix are fallible creatures in their own right. Gears of War 4 excelled in making such an iconic symbol of video game masculinity seem vulnerable, but failed to pull the trigger where it mattered most.

articles.headline: EA Offices Tagged With ‘Save Mass Effect’ Graffiti
keyFacts: Fans vandalized EA offices in Madrid with Save Mass Effect graffiti following the closure of BioWare.
Players previously bought a Times Square ad and started a petition that surpassed a quarter million signatures.
Politician Avi Lewis said stricter policies and federal funding should be used to protect and rebuild Canadian studios.
body: While evergreen to say that Mass Effect fans are having a rough go, itâs hard to imagine a worse couple of weeks. Earlier in the month, EA announced that they were closing BioWare, extinguishing any hope for a new entry along with it. Its most impassioned players have been incensed, to say the least, as one Reddit user stumbled across incidents of vandalism at one of the publisher’s offices.
“I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater,” posted Reddit user Ok_Link9625, “saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices.”

Scrawled in spray paint in front of the Madrid officeâs front gate and along one wall reads “SAVE MASS EFFECT.” Itâs an escalation in efforts to salvage the beloved series from an unceremonious end. A few days earlier, a number of fans banded together to purchase a 15 second ad spot in Times Square. This is all coupled by a petition on Change demanding that EA continue developing games in the series, with or without BioWare’s involvement. As of this writing, the petition has amassed well over a quarter million signatures. The Spanish office itself largely works on various EA Sports titles.

Fans are ultimately torn between these escalating tactics, whether itâs a ‘bad look’ for the community or simply a wasted effort. While the righteous indignation is understandable, itâs unlikely any of this will reverse course at the company. Amid their controversial acquisition from a coalition of Saudi and Jared Kushner-affiliated firms, Jason Schreierâs sources told him EA decided to abandon Mass Effect in favor of safer Star Wars tie-ins, such as Battlefront 3. EA in general is not known for caretaking their legacy franchises or studios, with BioWare in particular at the center of numerous labor disputes.

Even if these campaigns did catch an executiveâs ear, it wouldnât change the fact that EA shuttered the studio responsible for the series. The key damage has been done. Avi Lewis, the recently elected leader of the Canadian federal New Democratic Party, said that stricter policy should be implemented to keep private equity from mulching Canadian studios, going so far to say that BioWare staff should receive federal funding to rebuild the studio for themselves.

articles.headline: Federal judge bars DoJ from threatening election workers to stop processing ballots
keyFacts: A federal judge barred the Justice Department from threatening election workers to stop processing or counting ballots.
Civil rights groups and labor unions sued after the Trump administration demanded California segregate 20,000 ballots over citizenship allegations.
California's midterm election concludes on Tuesday, while officials said processed votes cannot be matched back to voters.
body: A federal judge has barred the justice department from threatening or coercing election workers to stop processing ballots.

The temporary restraining order issued by the US district judge Trina Thompson in the northern district of California late Friday also bars the justice department from demanding local election officials segregate or not count ballots that the federal government deems may have been illegally cast by immigrants, something that is exceedingly rare.
The order came the day after the justice department sent letters to election officials in all 50 states threatening to prosecute and jail any who failed to preserve ballot records.

The justice department’s “intimidation, threats, and attempts at coercion force election workers daily to choose between acceding to defendants’ unlawful demands or adhering to their duties and thereby subjecting themselves to a serious risk of criminal investigation and prosecution”. Thompson wrote.
The order in the lawsuit filed by labor unions and civil rights groups marks another blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to assert control over local elections.

It comes after a federal appeals court on Friday rejected the justice department’s request for California to set aside disputed ballots received in the midterm election, the latest setback for the Trump administration’s efforts to assert control over state-run elections.

The administration has alleged California sent ballots to about 20,000 people who may not be US citizens. It wants the state to set those ballots aside and not count them until citizenship can be verified. California officials say the list is highly unreliable and most likely includes many people who are US citizens.
A separate ruling from a three-judge panel on Wednesday forcefully denied that request, warning that the justice department’s demands could disenfranchise citizens.

“As the district court found – and we discern no clear error – there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the ninth circuit court of appeals panel wrote in its 2-1 ruling.
The majority opinion was authored by Judge Mark J. Bennett, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, and Judge Gabriel P. Sanchez, who was appointed by former Ppresident Joe Biden.

A justice department spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling. But in a statement about the sweeping efforts to root out noncitizen voting, it said: “Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting. Enforcing that law is not an agenda item. It is the Department’s job.”

Two data scientists from the University of California, Los Angeles recently found that more than 40% of the ballots flagged by the Trump administration bear names that are not even found on the state’s voter rolls, according to the Associated Press. The researchers found that the Trump administration flagged thousands of voters as ineligible, despite the fact that their names corresponded with those of US citizens.

Millions of people have already voted in California in the midterm election that concludes on Tuesday. Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. Elections officials have said that processed votes can’t be matched back to the voters who submitted them.
The top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, Bill Essayli, has said: “Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy.”
